rows.text: Heh, even though it's hard to guess what you are thinking, [Trailblazer]...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Perhaps it's time to fulfill my promise.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...So, [Trailblazer], you're saying you want to mass print the text of As I've Written and publish it as a book?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Not a bad idea. However, any publication on the Interastral Network must go through the IPC's channels. I'm not sure how they'd feel about this.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: We've already discussed the details of this project with the Business Consolidation Department. The verdict is: approved for execution.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Thanks to our experience in Jarilo-VI, we were able to close this deal. Rather than focusing on short-term gains, establishing a model of "Preservation" will be more beneficial for long-term development.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Besides, safeguarding new and growing civilizations is precisely what the Strategic Investment Department was made to do. According to Dr. Ratio, establishing a consistent understanding of Amphoreus across the cosmos will aid its future, to a certain degree.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: That's right. The Interastral Peace Entertainment will handle the publication of As I've Written, and the IPC will cover all related expenses.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: As for liaising with the various planets, we'll leave that to the Nameless.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: I see you've long been prepared. As expected of the "Throne of Worlds" of Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Perhaps soon it'll be time for the young ones to take charge of the Express.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Heh... Don't sound so world-weary, Welt. We've got plenty of youth left.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Even though the IPC is helping out, knowing you, you'd definitely want to go check it out yourself, right?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Go ahead then, and sow the seeds of civilization. Create a story that belongs to you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It's been a while, [Trailblazer]. I heard you were coming, so I invited Seele as well.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The kids at the orphanage are too scared to even go outside now because of the Destruction... Never mind that. What did you want to talk about?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Talk about As I've Written.
...I heard the whole cosmos was shaken up by what you did. Pretty impressive how you managed to sort everything out.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Thanks to Ms. Topaz's anti-Irontomb vaccine, and our timely shutdown of the Engine of Creation, Belobog was able to avoid another crisis.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Don't worry, the reconstruction plan hasn't been affected. But I must say... even a tiny ripple in the universe becomes a tsunami when it reaches frontier planets.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The same goes for Amphoreus. As a similarly developing civilization, we are willing to contribute to its future. Goodwill is like a torch. It can only burn brighter when it is passed on.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I'm not one for fancy words. But if you need help, I'll definitely be there.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Oh right, [Trailblazer]. I've got something to ask you. Come with me later.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Don't ask, just be there. I'm not playing around.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Honorary member! Finally, you're here! My legs are going numb...
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: Hook! What are you...
I heard from Clara that she was using Diggertron to help with mining, but the power was too much, and she fell and broke her leg. I'm afraid... she won't be able to take interstellar flights anymore.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: She wants to hear your fresh stories from beyond the sky, so she won't have any regrets.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Hmm... Just take it as the truth. Don't worry too much about the details.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Honorary member, you'll help Hook out, right?
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: Well, since you all say so...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Wowza~ Legends, galaxies, giant monsters... so cool!
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: I knew there are so many interesting things beyond the sky, but Julian and others wouldn't believe me! I'm gonna tell them right now!
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: Perhaps your story was so fascinating that it cured her without any treatment?
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Hehe... I admit I was just playing around earlier. She just wanted to see you. Children are all like that.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: All that fuss for nothing... Well, at least she's okay.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I should get going. Keep an eye on Hook. Make sure she doesn't pull any weird stunts...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: The children's energy seems endless. Ah, to be young...
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Haha, I couldn't snag another volume of As I've Written today either. Guess I still didn't show up early enough!
rows.speaker: Otakar

rows.text: You still have time to compete with us for books? Word on the street is that Irontomb infected a few old automatons... Isn't your Logistics Department supposed to handle that?
rows.speaker: Gina

rows.text: Wait, really?
How bad is it?
Shhhh! If everyone hears about this, it'll make the front page of Crystal Daily for sure!
rows.speaker: Otakar

rows.text: It did happen, but thankfully the folks at the Robot Settlement caught it in time before things got out of hand. The cleanup's gonna take several nights, and without a book to kill time, it's gonna be a real drag.
rows.speaker: Otakar

rows.text: You're in charge of military supplies, must've been pretty busy lately, huh?
rows.speaker: Otakar

rows.text: During the final battle with Irontomb, Fragmentum creations became increasingly active. I was assigned to guard duty at the restricted zone, and if I couldn't get my hands on another volume of As I've Written, I'd have nothing to do but freeze in my tent at night.
rows.speaker: Gina

rows.text: *sigh* A massive wave from the other edge of the universe would still cause quite a stir when it reaches here.
rows.speaker: Otakar

rows.text: Although Amphoreus seemed so distant from us, watching their struggles through each cycle, and seeing how the entire cosmos ultimately cast aside their differences to unite against the Destruction...
rows.speaker: Gina

rows.text: I feel like my efforts, though small, aren't completely insignificant after all.
rows.speaker: Gina

rows.text: If only I were a Chrysos Heir too! Like "Swift-Footed Cifera" I could just zoom home with godly speed after my shift and snuggle up in my cozy warm bed...
rows.speaker: Gina

rows.text: Wait wait, hold on. From what I've seen so far, she hasn't even shown up yet!
rows.speaker: Otakar

rows.text: Which volume did you all get?
This is just Volume 1.
rows.speaker: Otakar

rows.text: This is Volume 2.
rows.speaker: Gina

rows.text: Why don't you just swap with each other?
Who starts reading from the Volume 2?
Hehe, As I've Written is a hot potato right now. We're lucky to get our hands on any volume at all, who cares which one it is!
rows.speaker: Gina

rows.text: In that case, let's take turns reading it. But hey, no doodling or scribbling in the book, alright?
rows.speaker: Gina

rows.text: Perfect! Don't worry, Gina, I'll take good care of this book!
rows.speaker: Otakar

rows.text: By the way, that book seems really interesting. Would you mind sharing a copy with me? Next time a child is being difficult, I can use it to comfort them.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Feels like you're treating this like a fairy tale...
(cheer)
(keep silent)
Alright, alright!
rows.speaker: Agreeable Spectator

rows.text: Go on.
rows.speaker: Agreeable Spectator

rows.text: What's wrong with fairy tales? That story contains defiance, courage, and love. Exactly the qualities children should learn.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Besides, writing fairy tales is quite challenging. You must believe in the existence of beautiful things to write about them. In my opinion, sometimes adults need fairy tales even more than children do.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Since you've said so...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (cheer)
(keep silent)
Alright, alright!
rows.speaker: Agreeable Spectator

rows.text: Go on.
rows.speaker: Agreeable Spectator

rows.text: Through countless cycles of upheaval, As I've Written reveals the truth of Amphoreus. Want to know what happens next? Stay tuned for the next chapter!
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Thank you. Now, could you sign this for me? And add a little message too. There's a word for this... ah yes, book signing. Consider this practice for future book signings.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: (A message... what should I write?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (sigh)
(keep silent)
*sigh* This is so...
rows.speaker: Agreeable Spectator

rows.text: Go on.
rows.speaker: Agreeable Spectator

rows.text: May we meet again among the stars.
To everyone who dreams of being a hero.
This is the story of Amphoreus.
One, two, three, four, five... Dan Heng and Voidranger jive.
Well written indeed. This makes me the first owner of your exclusively signed copy.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: (sigh)
(keep silent)
*sigh* This is so...
rows.speaker: Agreeable Spectator

rows.text: Go on.
rows.speaker: Agreeable Spectator

rows.text: Through countless cycles of upheaval, As I've Written reveals the truth of Amphoreus. Want to know what happens next? Stay tuned for the next chapter!
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: I will pass this book down through generations, five hundred years, a thousand years... As long as children keep growing up, and children's children have children, it will never be forgotten.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Today we shall not speak of Mydeimos, the Backlit Spirit Warden, nor of Phainon, the Flame-Chasing Harbinger of Light. We speak only of the Twelve Golden Immortals who struck against the Archlord, and what a battle it was! Heaven and earth quaked, the struggle was fierce and unyielding!
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: After all, some things must be remembered. Like "that" Supreme Guardian, like all the acts of defiance that occurred among the stars...
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: D—Dr. Natasha, I brought them! Where's that book? I can't remember all the details in it.
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: (cheer)
(keep silent)
Alright, alright!
rows.speaker: Agreeable Spectator

rows.text: Go on.
rows.speaker: Agreeable Spectator

rows.text: Well then, shall I tell you the story again?
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: The story says Amphoreus had six moons. Guess they didn't need to turn on the lights at night, huh?
rows.speaker: Luda

rows.text: But they had no Sun, only something called the "Dawn Device" mounted on the back of the tallest Engine of Creation.
rows.speaker: Anka

rows.text: Anka, you're only getting half the story again. It's not called the "Engine of Creation." It's called the "Titan"!
rows.speaker: Tania

rows.text: (sigh)
(keep silent)
*sigh* This is so...
rows.speaker: Agreeable Spectator

rows.text: Go on.
rows.speaker: Agreeable Spectator

rows.text: Can someone really carry the Sun on their back? I'm not some gullible kid you can fool.
rows.speaker: Tania

rows.text: I can testify. I carried that Sun myself once.
If you don't believe me, will you at least believe Boss Hook?
(sigh)
(keep silent)
*sigh* This is so...
rows.speaker: Agreeable Spectator

rows.text: Go on.
rows.speaker: Agreeable Spectator

rows.text: You carried the Dawn Device? Yeah right, and I could totally take on Uncle Svarog!
rows.speaker: Tania

rows.text: Hook's vouching for it... somehow that makes it even more suspicious!
rows.speaker: Tania

rows.text: You approach the control console, and the four control levers wiggle excitedly back and forth, as if waving at you.
But... will Belobog one day vanish from the universe like the Amphoreans did, leaving behind nothing except a book?
rows.speaker: Luda

rows.text: Trust me. Just tweak the ending a tiny bit to make it less perfect, and people will absolutely go crazy for it!
rows.speaker: Control Stick

rows.text: The control stick shakes, making loud creaking noises.
A vase with flowers in it. It looks quite expensive. As you approach, a languid voice echoes from within.
If that happens, we'll never get to eat popping candies again, or listen to Natasha's stories...
rows.speaker: Luda

rows.text: No more playing hide-and-seek, or cheering for big brother Luka at the arena...
rows.speaker: Tania

rows.text: The vase is immersed in its own world, completely silent.
The vintage dial phone stares at you, occasionally rolling its eyeballs like an owl.
Amphoreus hasn't disappeared!
I won't let Belobog disappear.
Riddlers need to get out of Penacony.
Yeah! If that day ever comes, I'll stand tall like the heroes of Amphoreus and protect everyone in Boulder Town!
rows.speaker: Anka

rows.text: Then, we can sign a trade... adornment with the Amphoreans, just like we did with Xianzhou!
rows.speaker: Anka

rows.text: Anke, you forgot the name again. It's called the Mutual Benefit Trade Agreement!
rows.speaker: Tania

rows.text: That's not the point! The point is, we can go to the hot springs in Okhema, ride dromases... and, I want to raise a little chimera!
rows.speaker: Anka

rows.text: But... can we really take an interstellar flight to Amphoreus like Boss Hook?
rows.speaker: Luda

rows.text: Taking the Astral Express isn't bad either!
Let the young folks keep stirring things up. Who knows? Maybe they will actually change the universe one day.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Before that, you need to grow up properly!
*sigh*... I really, really wish I could grow up faster!
rows.speaker: Anka

rows.text: I hear Fu Xuan was also in that battle...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: So, junior soror, great changes are coming. Why not join the Yuque as the Master Diviner? That way I could catch a breather too.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: General Yao Guang must be joking. If I stay on the Luofu, I'm sure to inherit the position of General. If I transfer to the Yuque, I'd be nothing but a mere Master Diviner for life. How could I not see which path holds more promise?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Junior soror's optimism is truly delightful. Looks like "Optimistic General" is a Luofu specialty. Your visitor's here, so I should get going.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: [Trailblazer]? What perfect timing. I was just about to visit the Astral Express. What's the matter?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: ...Before obtaining this book, I only knew that golden blood was reaped in this battle, and thus it was deemed a great victory. I did not know that within that golden blood lay such a stirring and tragic story.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: You mean Madam Herta held a "Society meeting" and six geniuses actually attended? That's the highest number in the Society's history!
rows.speaker: Jackson

rows.text: Even that "Lord of Silence" answered Madam Herta's call!? Just thinking about that scene... I—I'm gonna hyperventilate!
rows.speaker: Jackson

rows.text: Jackson, calm down. Take deep breaths. The vitals monitor shows that your respiratory alkalosis risk is skyrocketing.
rows.speaker: Office Assistant

rows.text: Heh, look at your heart rate spike! I've never seen such exciting data in any of your research reports.
rows.speaker: Ithaca

rows.text: Ithaca, what you lack most is the vision to see through the true nature of data.
rows.speaker: Jackson

rows.text: My heart was racing because an elegant research direction was taking shape in my mind.
rows.speaker: Jackson

rows.text: No one would be able to tell that.
All I see is a desperate scholar.
(Stop listening for now)
Oh? Tell me about it.
rows.speaker: Ithaca

rows.text: Listen up: I'll be using As I've Written as my research subject to explore the two-way interaction between mythology and history, providing a complete theoretical framework for the evolution of primitive civilizations.
rows.speaker: Jackson

rows.text: The legacy left behind by countless cycles is as precious as the data provided by the Simulated Universe. The organic composition of Titans and their creations, the city-state mechanisms involving the Chrysos Heirs, the interactive relationship between narrators and texts...
rows.speaker: Jackson

rows.text: It all still feels like yesterday...
What's all that gibberish?
(Stop listening for now)
Hmm, sounds decent. Then?
rows.speaker: Ithaca

rows.text: An academic blueprint spanning history, mythology, anthropology, and biology is gradually unfolding before my eyes...
rows.speaker: Jackson

rows.text: It shall be named "Amphoreology"!
rows.speaker: Jackson

rows.text: This name will stir up a storm in the waters of humanities that have been stagnant for several Amber Eras! I need only sit at the source like Kephale, and research topics and funding will flow like golden blood to thousands of scholars...
rows.speaker: Jackson

rows.text: Conference invitations will come pouring in, and I'll be the first to give a speech at the opening ceremony. During breaks, no one will dare touch the refreshments unless I make the first move!
rows.speaker: Jackson

rows.text: Since it's all make-believe anyway, couldn't you let your imagination run a little wilder?
rows.speaker: Ithaca

rows.text: On top of that, the conference organizers will generously cover all accommodation and travel expenses!
rows.speaker: Jackson

rows.text: Calm down, Jackson. Your risk of respiratory alkalosis is reaching critical levels. Calm down!
rows.speaker: Office Assistant

rows.text: Shortly after the fall of Irontomb, the Alliance gathered all the generals to discuss their next course of action. The records in this book should provide them with additional support.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Look, it's [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Male 1

rows.text: {F#She}{M#He} saved the universe this time.
rows.speaker: Male 2

rows.text: Our light!
rows.speaker: Female 1

rows.text: Belobog wasn't affected much, thank goodness.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I'm meeting Robin at the cockpit... She's not gonna pretend to be an Intellitron again, is she?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Welcome back to your post, Captain!
rows.speaker: Attendant

rows.text: This garden is the final page of As I've Written...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Rest assured, whether through opera, storytelling, or crosstalk... The Luofu never lacks ways to spread stories that capture people's hearts.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Besides, the Alliance has been fighting battles everywhere in recent years, and there's been plenty of tales about their valor and victories. The word "hero" already carries weight in people's hearts.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Keep going! It's like an unwritten rule among the Nameless: press forward and see it through to the end.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You recounted the story behind As I've Written, and the current state of the Amphoreus...

The faithful adaptation of this As I've Written within the Alliance is most definitely assured. But from what you've said, if we want it to be remembered throughout the cosmos, the Luofu alone may not be enough.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: This matter requires the Sky-Faring Commission's assistance. Go talk to Yukong, I will inform her of the full situation.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Back when I was a pilot, I used to go on adventures everywhere with my companions in our starskiff. Even though we always managed to get out of sticky situations, we'd inevitably get a stern talking-to when we returned.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: A crisis that engulfs half the cosmos is still "ordinary" to you... As expected from someone whose great skill breeds great courage.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: And what an unforgettable journey it is. I can tell you'll cherish this memory for a long time.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Is that so? Such wonderful memories... I'm actually getting a bit envious.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: "Memory" is quite a peculiar thing. Sometimes, I even think it's a prank by the {RUBY_B#Fuli}Glowswather{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: That day he left in disgrace, bearing thorns in apology. Today he returns, bathed in blood, triumphant. Kremnos, his homeland, lay all in ruin, split asunder by blazing fire that forged adamant.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Yet today we shall not speak of the Psychopomp of Aidonia, but of "Mydeimos, the Backlit Spirit Warden," and bears the byname Mydei. The name Mydei that signifies "a foe that no multitude could withstand," as well as "a foe whom none among ten thousand could overcome!"
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: The wind tore through the banners, and rain beat down upon the remnants of the army. Across the plain rose cries of sorrow, yet only the roar of the lion was heard. And you ask: What manner of man was this Mydei? He was the crown prince of Kremnos, cast off by his father, drifting for years upon the Sea of Souls, where he forged an indestructible body. Summoned by the Thousand-Faced Matriarch, he threw himself into the great cause of Flame-Chase.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Yes. The answer was crystal clear from the start. The story of the three Nameless is the best proof of that, isn't it?

Thereafter, he hewed down the black tide, passed the trial, drank the crimson brew of blood, drove back the calamitous star of misfortune. He settled old grievances, guarded the holy city, reclaimed his sunken homeland, and ascended the Agate Throne.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Now this is epic: Like a battle-hardened lion on its throne, Kremnos's mighty name shall echo through the ages.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: You recounted the story behind As I've Written, and the current state of the Amphoreus...
Once he left his homeland, and for a hundred years he wandered in exile. Again came the cycle of a thousand tribulations, the return of ten thousand flames to one.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Today, we shall not speak of Mydeimos, the Backlit Spirit Warden, but of the "Lord Phainon, the Flame-Chasing Harbinger of Light." Born in a humble village of bucolic background, Lord Phainon rose from the most modest beginnings. Alas, the merciless black tide ravaged the countryside, leaving nothing but ruins, and he alone survived.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Lord Phainon first apprenticed under the Sages of the Grove, and later followed the Thousand-Faced Matriarch. Carrying the sun and chasing flame, he sought out the twelve Coreflames. Through countless trials and tribulations, he at last won the chance to remake the world.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Yet who could have foreseen that the prophecies inscribed on countless pages were but empty delusions, that the grand feats of salvation proved vain? The endless cycles of mortal birth and death became naught but the fertile soil that nourished the "Irontomb."
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: This stubborn youth, unwilling to serve as the wolf's thrall, began anew, setting forth once more upon the endless road of Flame-Chase. He entered the cycle again, taking flames into his own flesh as kindling.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: And truly it was thus: Startled, he turned his head only to behold a wasteland of shattered stone and broken tiles. All had perished, all was spent.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: The young girl smiled faintly. She had foreseen that at this moment you would hesitate, sigh, or pose a question.
Returning in vain, he found yet again the heavy heads of ripened grain, the cooking smoke curling beneath the slanting sun. And dusk was near once more.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: You recall the promise of Trailblaze: the story of Flame-Chase will echo across the stars. People will remember that Amphoreus was a brilliant, magnificent world.

With but one command, the Nine Heavens answered, and the three armies marched across the distant Cosmos. Heroes of heaven and earth joined their strength, and the Irontomb was ground to dust, its bones scattered and destroyed.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Tell me, my friends, what manner of adversary was this Irontomb? It was the creation of the Wisdomwalker, seized by the Ruin Author, who planted within it the seed of Destruction. When that seed at last sprouted, it threatened to bring upon the cosmos a calamity not seen for a thousand years.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Today, let us recount this tale in full detail.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: As the tale left off, under the call of the successor to the Cloudstrider, the IPC, the Geniuses, the Tuners, and even the great army of the Cloud Knights all gathered for this campaign, vowing to utterly annihilate the great foe.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: It was a world on the brink of extinction, yet teeming with heroes. In the Flame-Chase Journey, the Chrysos Heirs marched on one after another, while mortals stood united. This is an ode celebrating humanity, a hero's journey.

It is a world bound by cycles, yet also one that never surrenders. Even through eternal suffering, people will walk the same path and make the same choices. Transcending time itself, it is the true "Eternal Land."
It was a world born of conspiracy and sin, yet burned away alongside "Destruction." Before the cold and heavy destiny, it did not fall. But destiny itself did.
And of that spectacle, one might truly say: The starry sea stretched vast, no void within. A thousand sails pressed forward, filling every harbor.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Before your arrival, Amphoreus was virtually unknown. Thanks to the Express, it broke free from its cage and raced toward the stars.

For the first time, you faced a Lord Ravager head-on. Unlike in the Xianzhou, the cost of this battle was far too hefty. The threat of the Antimatter Legion is no longer just a flickering light in the distant stars.

As a member of the Flame-Chasers, you've joined Amphoreus's grand journey. You've encountered heroes, forged bonds, and achieved greatness together. As a traveler, your footprints have already reached far and wide.

In the heart of Amphoreus, Lord Phainon restrained the enemy with his very body, while the Twelve Golden Immortals fought it in a battle to the death. Golden threads shimmered and drifted, blades and sword-lights flashed like lightning, arrows split the air, fists flew in a deadly dance. Then came storms and tempests, wondrous arts and cunning stratagems, spearpoints like swimming dragons, and lethal chess plays.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Yet Irontomb bore within it the rage of thirty million lifetimes... Who could stand against such an adversary? Alas, alas! Vengeful rain and hateful clouds veiled the heavens, the three armies were destroyed, and all was brought to ruin.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Good sirs and ladies, at that brink of life and death, who do you think turned back the tide? It was the successor of the Cloudstrider, the Gray Savior, bearing the memories of thirty million lifetimes, wielding the power of trillions of golden Coreflames, who struck down the enemy just as it neared completion.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Yet, alas, after all has been said and done about the endless cycle, all that remained was but a flash across the cosmos, thousands upon thousands of memories dissolving into a single page of story. Amphoreus returned then to its origin.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Don't worry, we have allies.

That sky-shrouding giant tree, the suspended peak of Kremnos, the hero's bath flowing with golden blood... One day, this splendid vision shall reappear in the universe. But, though our lifespans be long, I fear it shall be left for later generations to behold.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Good sirs and ladies, the countless turns of Amphoreus's fate are now entrusted to our cheers and chatter. Should it be, when my final hour arrives, that this old man may join those Chrysos Heir heroes, and let the tale remember me on your behalf... Why, that would be a fine thing indeed.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Every great dream must end in waking, every grand play must have its curtain drawn. When the screen is drawn and the gavel struck, let us fold our arms and watch as idle spectators. Thus, the story comes to its close.
rows.speaker: Zhen Delin

rows.text: Mikhail always welcomes visitors. For those who lose their way, he never fails to point them in the right direction.
rows.speaker: Micah

rows.text: But there's no confusion in your expression. I'm guessing you're not here for answers.
rows.speaker: Micah

rows.text: That's right. I went to a world that even Akivili never reached, and accomplished an unprecedented "Trailblaze"...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: That's right. During my journey, I met many fellow pathstriders and made precious memories...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: That's right. Together with another author, I wrote a book about the Trailblaze journey. This time, I'm here to tell that story...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I want to share this experience with those who came before.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Time is of the essence. You head to Belobog...
Alright, alright. Let's tell them what kind of story this really is.
rows.speaker: Micah

rows.text: (Let's start with the world of Amphoreus.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (And now, for the meaning of this journey...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Did Mikhail feel the same way when he stayed in Penacony back then?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Destruction, Nihility, Harmony, and...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (But the stars will remember the name of every epic.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Looks like this Trailblaze...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I've made up my mind. Let me start from the beginning...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: News doesn't travel as fast in dreams. Every plot twist in this story caught me completely off guard.
rows.speaker: Micah

rows.text: Thanks, I guess that's all that needs to be said.
rows.speaker: Micah

rows.text: I think Mikhail would be proud of you all.
rows.speaker: Micah

rows.text: The journey against the Destruction, and the stories behind it, should be known by more people.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I know a few publishers who can make dream bubbles based on sample books and put them on the market in Penacony. However...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: As you know, Penacony is a realm wrapped in syrup. I worry that epic tales of heroes might be too heavy for those living in dreams.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: You retell the story of As I've Written to Hook sentence by sentence, especially those thrilling adventure parts. Naturally, done in the voice of a bath sprite.
All we can do is put it on the shelf. Whether it survives the competition... there are too many uncertainties...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: But I think, [Trailblazer], you should just follow what your heart tells you. People can only tell stories they truly believe in.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Hook sprang up from the bed with a "whoosh" and dashed away in a flash.
Once you've made up your mind, go see Dr. Edward. I'll convince Mr. Oti to help out. See you later!
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Dear captain, do you remember me? I've been watching you for quite a while...
rows.speaker: Expensive Vase

rows.text: Tell me your story, and I'll teach you about niche art. As long as you immerse yourself in your own world, you won't get hurt.
rows.speaker: Expensive Vase

rows.text: Captain, did you know that I wasn't always a dial phone? I used to be an owl. But I'm not an owl anymore, I'm a dial phone.
rows.speaker: Dial Phone

rows.text: Wanna take a guess why? If you know, you know. And if you don't, well, no amount of explaining will help.
rows.speaker: Dial Phone

rows.text: Captain, look at me! I'm the control stick, and I'm an expert at controlling hearts!
rows.speaker: Control Stick

rows.text: Love, friendship, rage, regret... Such a tiny dream bubble contains such complex emotions. It's like pouring a whole bottle of vodka into a dolium.
rows.speaker: Dr. Edward

rows.text: You recounted the story behind As I've Written, and the current state of the Amphoreus...
Thank you for providing the memories. Here's my verdict: It's bound to be a huge hit.
rows.speaker: Dr. Edward

rows.text: Even if the results aren't what we expected, I can still have the heroes tap dance in the Vortex of Genesis. That'll be just as big a success.
rows.speaker: Dr. Edward

rows.text: Haha, just kidding. Rest assured. I'm a professional dream bubble collector. I know what can and can't be successful.
rows.speaker: Dr. Edward

rows.text: And so, As I've Written was published in Penacony.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Some guessed the Alfalfa was behind it, and they weren't wrong. With such a big favor ready for the taking, why not use it?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Titans, cycles, "Fall of the Erudition"... Quite the imagination there.
rows.speaker: James

rows.text: Too bad the plot is so cliché! It's just another story about heroes fighting monsters! We've seen that a hundred times already!
rows.speaker: James

rows.text: That's what you call a classic formula. People keep coming back for more, and that's why this theme never gets old.
rows.speaker: Cathy

rows.text: Not to mention this was based on a real story...
rows.speaker: Cathy

rows.text: Haven't you heard the Interastral Peace Broadcast? Irontomb was really defeated, and the seeds of civilization have sprouted in the universe.
rows.speaker: Cathy

rows.text: Maybe we'll be able to step into that memoria world one day and have face-to-face conversations with the heroes from that book.
rows.speaker: Cathy

rows.text: In Penacony, dreams must conform to reality, and As I've Written is no exception.
What will you choose? Lucky for you, this is a dreamscape where furniture can talk. Why not hear what they have to say?
A world made of memoria? No way. That's gotta be something the Oak Family made up.
rows.speaker: James

rows.text: Whatever. Just go hang out with Clockie at the theme park, and watch out for those alien memes trying to abduct you.
rows.speaker: Cathy

rows.text: The researchers are still as busy as ever. Yep, this is the space station I know.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Right. Let's send the damaged ships to Pier Point and have the IPC foot the bill...
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Oh, if it isn't [Trailblazer]. Perfect timing. I've got good news and bad news. Which would you like to hear first?
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Hmm... Now that I think about it, starting with the bad news might be a bit too abrupt. Let me give you the good news first.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Remember that starnought I gave you? The good news is that I got one from a space pirate...
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: But his fleet was dispatched to fight against the Irontomb, and that starnought... was destroyed.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: I've reposted my purchase order. But it'll be tough to find another seller anytime soon for a ship of that size.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: ...I have to say that this idea is way more interesting than the researchers' projects. It's a shame you don't need funding, or I'd definitely invest a few hundred million credits.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: I took an elective called "History of Frontier Planets" back in my student days. The professor warned us on the first day not to take everything at face value.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Many worlds add exaggerated elements to their local hero legends, claiming their ancestors' bloodlines are inherited from some Aeon... Eventually, having an extraordinary origin story became quite the trend.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: But... isn't that how stories work? When enough people believe in them, they gradually become reality.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: I'll get As I've Written added to the space station's required reading list. The researchers may not be interested in mythology, but once they hear it's Madam Herta's project, they'll get as excited as Peppy seeing a spacesuit.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Speaking of which, where's Herta?
Madam Herta has... overexerted herself. She still needs some time to recover.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Who said that?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: So, what happened to Cyrene?
A mere Lord Ravager isn't enough to make me "overexert" myself. I just wasn't online, that's all.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: The IPC keeps pestering me about forming some "alliance." I got tired of their nagging, so I just turned on auto-answering mode.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oh right, [Trailblazer]. I've got some more good news. After Irontomb fell, the Scepter was ruined, but Screwy and I managed to salvage a majority of data.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: They are crucial for the newborn Amphoreus. Well, let's call it that for now. If things go smoothly, the world's evolution can skip its inorganic life phase and take a big step forward.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Besides, the last extrapolation record, the one when you acted as the Worldbearing Titan, is crucial. The Trailblaze will replace the Destruction and purify this world.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: How long until a new Amphoreus is born?
Screwy has signed a special agreement with the IPC. They will closely monitor the state of Amphoreus for a while.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: My advice is: continue the journey, be prepared for the worst, but keep hope in your heart. You know that if there's one thing the world of Amphoreus isn't short of, it's miracles.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: So what is the prime mover of life?
As the "heart" of the Scepter, she, too, filled the cosmos in the instant when Irontomb swept across all of existence. She became the memories of the stars.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: The surging Imaginary Energy enabled her to create a miracle. With {RUBY_B#the Remembrance}her self{RUBY_E#} as the cradle, she closed the cycle of causality in Amphoreus, making a world emerge from the Memory Zone.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Of course, I know you just want to hear the outcome. Let me put it this way. She's... just sleeping. Maybe she'll open her eyes again as a pink memosprite and once again embark on a journey to meet you...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: At last, your journey of sowing has reached its end, and you return to the Astral Express...
Looking back, the Amphoreus you spoke of has taken root deep across the universe, quietly awaiting the day it will sprout.
But that had already happened in the "past." In her subjective time, everything has become "eternal."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...She was smiling when she left you. So, don't be sad. She'd tell you the same if she were here.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I... can't make any promises. That planet will gradually become how you remember it to be, but no one can tell when that'd be.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: It might take a thousand Amber Eras, or it might only take a year or two. The only thing for certain is that what you are doing will surely hasten its growth.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Screwy and I have reached a consensus on that. Regrettably, the answer given by the Scepter is indeed "Destruction." You can find a more detailed discussion in the database.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: But that's not Amphoreus's answer, and I don't imagine it's yours either.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I have my own insights on this, which I've written in the annotations. If you're interested in this kind of stuff, you can make it your own research topic.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Then I'll disconnect for now. Got lots of stuff to deal with. Herta, signing off.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: The world has never been so quiet. It is as though you could hear the sound of heartbeats.
This is the final stroke you write for Amphoreus. Only fate knows when it will respond.
But you know, whether it's "tomorrow" or "the day after tomorrow," they're all on the path of the Trailblaze. Not as parallel lines, but as points destined to converge.
Madam Herta has actually been thinking about Amphoreus all this time. The last time she couldn't stop talking about something was when we contained the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Leave As I've Written to us. I'll contact you again when we have news.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: You see: The nebula blooms with radiance, tracing the silhouette of a garden. A newborn world is about to sprout.

This scene is the ending of As I've Written, and also the origin point of the Amphoreus in the real world: One day, it will give birth to true life. The people in the memory will be born one by one, waiting for you "tomorrow."
The stars breathe silently. You are certain that the fruit of Amphoreus has been planted.
But what about its "cause"? Until that day comes, the journey continues. Endless possibilities unfold beneath your feet, and only "the memory"...
Only "the memory" remains in yesterday.

You think: you can let more people read As I've Written, preserving the memories of this world. If you do this, the causality will become more stable... You can't be certain, but you're willing to believe.
What matters is that this is a promise, shared between you and many others.
Perhaps this is the final step of "Genesis."
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: What are you spacing out for?
Of course! After all, we three trailblazed through Amphoreus together. I ran my heart out for this!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I received a message from March when I was leaving Thalassa, so I came back with her. She ran into some trouble on Kalsas.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yeah, so much has happened in Amphoreus. How could I sum it all up in just a few words? This story... I'm afraid it's going to take a while...
Don't even get me started. I'm already shy as it is, and then the Synesthesia Beacon had to break down... Thank goodness Dan Heng can speak the Clayese language.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: "Trailblaze" isn't just about moving forward, it's also the responsibility of connecting worlds. After this stop, you seem to better understand the conviction behind Akivili's departure.
Also, I discovered a new species resembling chimeras on Spindle-III. There were no prior records of it.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Be it Mikhail or any Navigator before, each era's Trailblaze has its own significance. And the fog that stands in your way seems to be getting clearer...
Does that mean there could be planets completely filled with dromases?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Such is the way of the Trailblaze. Explore, understand, build, and connect. But there's always a next stop on this journey. When the whistle of departure sounds, the Express will leave, carrying all memories with it.
Let's wait for Himeko and Mr. Yang to come back before we do a full debrief. You should rest for now, [Trailblazer], you look tired.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You spent countless moments in this dream within a dream. As the story ended, a certain emotion in your heart grew stronger, like a burning ember.
Yeah. See you in a bit then!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Stay strong. Eyes forward, always ♪
See you tomorrow, Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]
